title: run_venture_tests --times read a ten-day-old file and ranked suites perf runs had already fixed
problem: venture_suite_times.json was taken 2026-11-17 and nothing said it was stale; perf runs steering by `--times` saw suites with 6-12 perf passes since at the top and spent time on dead ends.
evidence: full re-run 2026-11-28 (4 jobs, 4 cores, ~25 min): shed-designer 472 -> 249 s, chant-forge 39 -> 128 s, changepoint-detector 153 -> 757 s (tests added 2026-11-24), 1365 -> 1447 suites
change: `--times` prints a STALE line once the file is 7+ days old, with the refresh commands, and marks rows whose latest perf write-up postdates the timing '(after timing: re-time)'. The file was refreshed from a full run in the same PR.
metric: run-record doc_friction naming run_venture_tests.py --times as stale, in the 5 days after the merge
